d: Paramount estimates $31M from 3,575 theaters, plus $20.1M overseas for a $51.1M worldwide start. That's No. 1, and a solid start rather than a breakout. Audiences gave it a B- CinemaScore.

t: Clayface opens No. 1 with $24M
d: DC's horror spin took $24M at 3,458 theaters with an A- CinemaScore, per Deadline's Sunday estimates. You Can See Everything was second with $19.5M ($45.1M total) and Wildwood third with $11.6M.

t: Narnia: The Magician's Nephew trailer
d: Greta Gerwig's Narnia, scored to Stairway to Heaven, with Meryl Streep voicing Aslan. Big swing. Our take: it works.

t: Other Mommy slides to third
d: Last weekend's winner made an estimated $8.35M in weekend two, down 70%, for $44.85M total. New openers Whalefall ($8M against $10M to $12M tracking) and Sense and Sensibility ($7.25M) came in soft.

t: The Pinterest vibe check
d: Search singer, vinyl, season and character on Pinterest, screenshot the first image for each, and post the grid. It's your algorithm's read on you, in four squares, and it's weirdly accurate.

t: Halloween costume rankings are in
d: Witches and vampires top NRF's survey of what adults will wear, Spider-Man rules for kids, and Google's trending list is led by Buddy the Unicorn and NeeDoh. Halloween is Saturday, Oct 31.

t: Olivia Rodrigo x Chappell Roan "expectations"
d: Olivia's first-ever remix and Chappell's first-ever feature, out now. The video is a retro game show hosted by David Byrne. Yes, really.

t: Tate McRae's "Housewife"
d: Her first new music since So Close To What: a synth-pop independence anthem with a video shot in the South of France. Fans are chanting the money line everywhere, and she was on the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show lineup Sunday.

t: Harry Styles sings for Liam Payne
d: On the second anniversary of Liam Payne's death, Harry debuted an unreleased song he wrote for his friend, "What Is Enough," at Madison Square Garden. "It's just about looking after each other," he told the crowd.

t: Miley's tearful Dolly tribute
d: At her Hollywood Bowl show for the new album Bass Persuades on Oct 16, Miley Cyrus honored her late godmother Dolly Parton before singing "Jolene": "Me and Dolly, we are eternal."

t: Taylor Swift's "Patient Zero"
d: Second straight week at No. 1 on the Hot 100. Her 16th chart-topper. TikTok is using it for wedding edits.

t: Drake & Don Toliver debut at No. 5
d: New collab, straight into the Hot 100 top 5. Also on that chart: ADÉLA's first top 10.

t: "we fell in love in october"
d: girl in red's song is still one of the fastest-climbing TikTok sounds, with 2M+ videos. Peak fall.

t: Grammy nominations
d: The 2027 nominees drop Monday, Nov 16. The ceremony is Feb 7 on ABC, Disney+ and Hulu.

t: Rays walk off, force Game 5
d: Tampa Bay beat Milwaukee 4-3 in 12 innings on Ben Williamson's pinch-hit single, minutes after Cooper Pratt's go-ahead homer. Brewers lead 3-1; Game 5 is tonight, 8 p.m. ET on FOX.

t: Rays win the pennant
d: Díaz and Junior Caminero homered and Freddy Peralta went 5 1/3 strong as Tampa Bay beat Cleveland 7-3 in Game 6 to take the ALCS 4-2. It's the Rays' third World Series trip, after 2008 and 2020.

t: Valkyries lead WNBA Finals 3-2
d: Golden State can clinch Thursday. Game 6 tips at 12:30 p.m. ET at State Farm Arena in Atlanta on USA and Peacock, moved up from 8 p.m. so it could be held in the bigger arena, per NBC Sports.

t: Sixers spoil the Knicks' banner night
d: The Knicks raised their title banner, then Philadelphia won 106-100 at MSG. Tyrese Maxey scored 28, Jaylen Brown had 19 in his Sixers debut and LeBron James added 14, 9 and 7 to open his record 24th season. Detroit rallied from 22 down to beat Boston 121-113, and OKC beat San Antonio 116-104.

t: NHL: where to watch
d: 84-game season, split between ESPN and TNT. Sunday's Heritage Classic: Canadiens 2, Jets 1, as Jacob Fowler made 33 saves outdoors in Winnipeg.

t: AEW WrestleDream: Ospreay survives
d: Will Ospreay kept the AEW World title in the first-ever Clockwork Carnage match in Orlando, finishing with 3 points to 2 each for Adam Copeland, Samoa Joe and Darby Allin.

t: Google Gemini 4 Argon
d: Google's new frontier model, out Oct 13 with a 1M-token window. It's pitched as less hedgy and less cliché.

t: Open-source AI keeps moving
d: Frontier labs went closed this week (hello, Muse Wonder). Open-weight models and small labs are still the other half of the story.

t: Meta Muse Wonder
d: Meta's first frontier model. Not open-weight this time, which is a big shift from Llama.

t: Microsoft Maia 300 chip
d: Microsoft's third in-house AI chip. The pitch: 40% better performance per megawatt. Deployment is planned for 2027.

t: ChatGPT Voice gets GPT-Live-1.1
d: OpenAI is rolling out GPT-Live-1.1 in ChatGPT Voice with more natural accents and new voices for French, German, Hindi, Japanese, Korean and Mexican Spanish. Developers can now design a custom voice from a text prompt.

t: iPhone Duo is on sale
d: Apple's first foldable is out today, but walk-in stock is limited and delivery dates slipped to late January within minutes of preorders opening, Reuters reports. Reviews praise the hinge but note there's no telephoto lens.

t: Copper & cherry-cola hair
d: Pinterest's first Beauty Trend Report says hair is going warm and moody: mocha, copper, cherry cola.

t: Ghost Rose nails
d: Milky, blush-nude nails beating burgundy this fall. Quiet but very chic.

t: Smoky eyes + burgundy lips
d: Clean girl is taking a night off. Runways from Saint Laurent to Gucci brought the smoke back.

t: Victoria's Secret names a new Angel
d: Solange Omon, 21, won the Angels Among Us search and made her runway debut at Sunday's show in Los Angeles, with an IMG Models contract. The other headline: Kylie Jenner walked in the $50 million Fantasy Bra, the first Fantasy Bra on the runway since 2018.

t: Kylie Jenner's $50 million Fantasy Bra
d: Jacob & Co. built it with 4,410 diamonds around a 75.54-carat Fancy Vivid yellow diamond. It took 15 craftspeople more than 1,000 hours, weighs just under four pounds, and at $50 million it's the priciest Fantasy Bra ever, per Vogue.

t: Taco Bell x Milk Bar Birthday Cake Empanada
d: Out now nationwide. Cake-flavored empanada with pink frosting and sprinkles. $3.49. Chaotic in the best way.

t: Wingstop x Sour Patch Kids wings
d: Wings in a sour-then-sweet glaze. We're scared. We're also going.

t: Dunkin' Spider Donut is back
d: The Halloween Spider Donut returns, plus a purple Berry Battie drink.

t: Popeyes x Megan Thee Stallion
d: A new Honey Chicken Biscuit with a Megan Thee Stallion merch tie-in.

t: The "Six Seven" dance
d: A Brazilian funk track: count on your fingers, shrug on the drop. J-Hope did it and the top video hit 75M+ views.

t: Ramalama costume walk
d: A creepy low-angle shot zooms out to reveal the Halloween fit, set to Róisín Murphy. Easy to copy, hard to stop watching.

t: Pumpkin Head Illusion
d: Hold a pumpkin up to the lens and congratulations, you're a pumpkin. Spooky-season gold.

t: Your sixth photo killed you
d: Open your camera roll, find the sixth picture, and post it as your mock "cause of death." Geckos, toilet-paper dogs and crash-test cars so far. Started Oct 16 and spread fast.

t: Start of COVID vs. now
d: Side-by-side photos from lockdown days next to 2026 mirror selfies: gym glow-ups, beards, brand-new hair. Some proud, some hilarious, all very this weekend.

t: AI cat melodrama
d: Synthetic cats acting out family dramas and tiny tragedies. Weirdly emotional, and a fast-breaking format.

t: Midterms: 6 days out
d: Every House seat, 35 Senate races and 36 governor races are on the ballot Tuesday, Nov 3. Early voting is underway in many states, and dates differ by state, so check your own before you go.

t: Shutdown watch: the real deadline is Dec 11
d: No shutdown in October. The stopgap law signed Sept 2 (H.R. 6500) funds the government through Friday, Dec 11, 2026, so the next deadline lands in the lame-duck session after the Nov 3 election. Key dates and what a shutdown would mean for Social Security, mail and parks.

t: White House press secretary out after 5 days
d: Katie Zacharia is leaving the press secretary job after five days, NBC News reports. A senior official says she's moving to a new role. It followed criticism of her first briefing and her acknowledgment that she did not pass the bar exam. She thanked the president in a statement.

t: 60 Minutes on the people who count the votes
d: Lesley Stahl's Sunday report, "The Vote," looked at federal actions affecting state and local election officials ahead of Nov 3, including an FBI search of a Fulton County, Georgia election warehouse and Justice Department requests for voter rolls. It featured Utah Lt. Gov. Deidre Henderson and Justice Department official Harmeet Dhillon, so both state officials and DOJ gave their side.

t: Lame-duck to-do list
d: After the election, Congress gets about 24 legislative days. On the list: funding past Dec 11, the defense policy bill, and farm and surveillance reauthorizations.

t: SCOTUS: Beaird v. United States
d: Can courts still defer to Sentencing Commission commentary after Loper Bright? Justices from both wings sounded skeptical of changing the rule. A decision is due by July.

t: SCOTUS: Salazar v. Paramount Global
d: This week's argument asked how far the Video Privacy Protection Act reaches. It matters for every site that embeds video.

t: U.S. allows Russian diesel sales through April 2027
d: Treasury issued a temporary license letting Russian diesel be sold through April 2027, AP reports. President Trump says it will help lower fuel prices and push Russia toward talks. Zelenskyy called it a weak decision that helps Moscow and urged Americans to back reinstating the sanctions, and the Kremlin welcomed the move.

t: France: 2,400 arrests after a weekend of riots
d: Saturday's cost-of-living marches drew about 550,000 people, and arrests from the weekend's violence and looting have climbed to about 2,400, including 351 in Paris. Macron called for calm and refused Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's resignation, and the prime minister is holding a crisis meeting.

t: UK sends Typhoon jets to help defend Saudi Arabia
d: Britain is deploying RAF Typhoons in a defensive role after weeks of Houthi strikes on Saudi cities and oil sites, the BBC reports. The UK defense secretary said the jets will not carry out offensive strikes. Several airlines have paused flights to the region.

t: Hormuz: more ships hit, Brent tops $112
d: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it struck four vessels in the northern Gulf and that three more ships hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent jumped 3.83% to $112.99 on Thursday. The New York Times reports U.S. and Israeli military planning for possible renewed strikes on Iran after the midterms.

t: Ebola: Kenya at nine cases, Nigeria confirms one
d: Kenya's health ministry now counts nine confirmed cases of Bundibugyo virus disease, a type of Ebola, including one death, all in a single cluster of people already in quarantine. Nigeria confirmed one imported case in Abuja on Oct 20, a traveler from Uganda now in isolation, with 44 contacts being monitored. The CDC has entry rules for U.S.-bound travelers from affected countries.

t: Japan's 9.9 quake alert that wasn't
d: Japan's weather agency sent an emergency alert for a magnitude 9.9 quake on Oct 16, then withdrew it about eight minutes later. The real quake was a 6.9 near Kamchatka. JMA apologized, explained the error and denied any cyberattack.

t: Tesla x SpaceX merger talk
d: A Barclays note says a Tesla-SpaceX merger could be announced before Tesla's December annual meeting, and Musk's "Tesla x SpaceX" post poured fuel on it. Nothing has been announced.

t: FMC plunges 31%
d: The crop-chemicals maker slashed its Q3 outlook, blaming weak demand, pricey inventory sitting with distributors and cheaper generics. Shares hit a multi-decade low.

t: Barclays cools on Dell and HPE
d: Barclays cut both to hold, questioning when enterprise AI spending really shows up. Dell fell 6.8% and HPE 7.1% on Oct 15.

t: Bumble to be acquired for $1.3B
d: The dating-app company agreed to an all-cash deal with Ithaca Holdings, according to its SEC filing.

t: Social Security COLA is 3.6%
d: It's official: Social Security and SSI rise 3.6% in 2027. About 76 million Americans. SS payable January 2027; SSI from Dec 31, 2026. Taxable max $192,300. Biggest bump in three years.

t: Medicare open enrollment is open
d: Oct 15 through Dec 7: compare 2027 Medicare Advantage and Part D plans. Changes take effect Jan 1. Different from HealthCare.gov open enrollment (that opens Nov 1).

t: Gas eases to $4.29
d: AAA's national average for regular was about $4.29 on Oct 19, down 6 cents in a week and 18 cents in a month, even with U.S. crude still above $100. Diesel is still far above last year's price.

t: Mortgage rates hold at 7.40%
d: Freddie Mac's 30-year average didn't budge this week and is still at a three-year high. The next reading is Thursday, Oct 22.

t: Flu shot: aim for end of October
d: CDC says everyone 6 months and older should get a flu shot, ideally by the end of October. People 65+ should get the high-dose types.

t: COVID vaccine guidance
d: CDC's current COVID shot guidance is a shared decision with your provider. It's especially important for 65+ and high-risk people.

t: Porsche Mission S
d: Porsche revealed a mid-engined super sports car concept on the same Queens pier where the 550 Spyder debuted in 1953. A production version will sit above the 911. Engine and price: not announced.

t: Ford's 4.38M-vehicle recall
d: A trailer-brake-control recall covering F-Series, Ranger, Maverick and Lincoln models. Check your VIN.

t: Jeep & Wagoneer TPMS recall
d: About 202,000 SUVs whose tire-pressure monitors may not warn you.

t: The 12-foot Skelly returns
d: Home Depot's giant skeleton is back, now with app-controlled moves and LCD eyes. $299 original, $379 upgraded.

t: Cats are catching up
d: Dogs still lead at 88.9M to 77M cats, but more US households now own kittens than puppies.

t: Cat vet visits up, dog visits down
d: Feline clinic visits rose 2.7% in Q3 while dog visits fell.

t: The 2027–28 FAFSA is open
d: It went live Sept 23, the earliest launch ever. Some aid is first-come, first-served, so file early.

t: Peak leaf season
d: New England is peaking now. The Midwest and Mid-Atlantic follow mid-to-late October, and the Southeast peaks into early November.

t: Santa Ana winds fade, rain on the way
d: NWS Los Angeles says all red flag warnings and heat advisories have expired. A big cool-down starts today, and 0.25 to 1 inch of rain is very likely Wednesday and Thursday, so watch for mud and debris flows near burn scars.

t: East Coast storm watch
d: A storm-force low is sitting a few hundred miles off the Southeast coast, and the National Hurricane Center says high winds, coastal flooding and dangerous surf are expected along parts of the East Coast over the next few days. It has a 40% chance of turning subtropical this week as it pulls away.

t: Blueface proposes to Chrisean Rock
d: A nightclub proposal in Scottsdale, complete with a bottle-girl sign. She said yes.

t: Academy Museum Gala: Taylor Swift closes the night
d: Taylor Swift performed at the sixth Academy Museum Gala in LA on Oct 17, in a pale-blue Dior gown. Rosé went sheer Saint Laurent with a giant bow. The honorees were Charlize Theron, Colman Domingo and John Carpenter.

t: Pauly D is engaged
d: The Jersey Shore star and Nikki Hall got engaged in Vegas after six years together.

t: Tobey Maguire officiates ex's wedding
d: Jennifer Meyer married Geoffrey Ogunlesi in Hawaii, and her ex Tobey Maguire officiated. Peak co-parenting energy.

t: Hinge is eating Tinder's lunch
d: Hinge's payers grew 17% while Tinder's fell 5%. Dating is shifting from swipes to intentional.

t: App fatigue is real
d: Reviewers say singles want fewer swipes and more verified, IRL-first apps.

t: #CityTasteTest
d: Honest local food reviews, city by city. TikTok's favorite format this month for small spots.

t: Format fragmentation
d: No single mega-challenge this month. Instead, lots of micro-trends: costume transitions, K-pop revivals, cat edits.

t: Tesla beats on profit, stock slips
d: Adjusted EPS of $0.48 topped the $0.43 estimate and revenue hit $28.05B, but car revenue fell 3% and free cash flow dropped 62%. Shares fell more than 3% after hours. Musk called a SpaceX merger a good idea; nothing is agreed. Not investment advice.

t: Meta slides 8% on AI spending
d: Revenue jumped 26% to $64.6B, but Meta raised its 2026 capex plan to $135B to $145B, free cash flow went negative and it unveiled a nonvoting Class C stock. Shares fell 7.84% on Thursday. Not investment advice.

t: Moderna gives some back
d: After a big run, Moderna fell 7.82% to $218.01 on Oct 16 as traders took profits ahead of full Phase 3 melanoma vaccine data due Oct 24. Not advice.

t: Dow drops 1.2% Friday
d: The Dow fell 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to 52,215.16 on Friday. The S&P 500 slipped 0.52% to 7,623.68 and the Nasdaq dipped 0.21% to 25,955.34, per AP. Not investment advice.

t: Norte Fire: evacuations lifted
d: All evacuation orders for the Norte Fire in south Orange County were lifted by Saturday evening, with the fire at 570 acres and 25% contained. Some roads and the burn area stay closed.

t: Bend, Oregon school shooting
d: Police say a 16-year-old forced his way into Silver Rail Elementary on Thursday and killed three children and a teacher. A teacher fought him and a parent shot him, AP reports. The school district has a community hub with support resources.

t: Open enrollment 2027
d: HealthCare.gov opens Nov 1. Enroll by Dec 15 for Jan 1 coverage. It closes Jan 15.

t: SpaceX CRS-35 docked at the ISS
d: Dragon arrived Oct 15 with 6,300+ lbs of cargo, including the station's final roll-out solar arrays.

t: Artemis III booster stacked
d: NASA finished stacking the boosters for the Moon-landing mission, with all four RS-25 engines installed.

t: Gulf flights paused
d: Delta, Lufthansa, Air France-KLM and Qatar Airways were among the airlines that suspended flights to Saudi Arabia and nearby countries after strikes on Riyadh's airport. Check your airline before you go.

t: Boeing 737 MAX 10 is certified
d: The FAA certified the largest 737 MAX on Oct 20 after years of delays. It seats up to 230, adds an enhanced angle-of-attack system and was the first jet certified under the full 2020 safety law. WestJet is the launch customer, with service expected in early 2027.

t: Japan launches MMX to a moon of Mars
d: JAXA's MMX lifted off on an H3 rocket on Oct 20 and is healthy after its first critical operations. It reaches Mars orbit in August 2027, drops a French-German rover on Phobos, grabs samples and brings them home in July 2031. A world first.

t: Google Cloud outage knocks out Revolut
d: A power event in Google Cloud's London region on Oct 20 took down Revolut's app, cards and transfers worldwide for hours, and hit other UK sites too. Google says it's resolved and Revolut says customers' money and data stayed safe.

t: Netflix beats, guides light
d: Q3 revenue rose 11.8% to $12.87B and EPS was $0.87, ahead of the $0.82 consensus. But Q4 guidance of $0.67 a share missed, the ad forecast dropped to about $2.7B, and shares fell about 5% after hours. Coming up: Cliff Booth, the Emily in Paris finale and Christmas NFL games.

t: Storm Adam floods eastern Spain
d: At least six people have died and more than 2,000 were evacuated as Storm Adam flooded parts of Valencia and Alicante. Rescue teams are still searching marshland near Pego and Oliva.

t: Kremlin says Ukraine talks could resume
d: After Vladimir Putin met U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff, Kremlin officials said they would agree to resume U.S.-brokered talks next month, the first since February. Overnight Russian strikes hit 12 Ukrainian regions including Kyiv, and Russia reported Ukrainian drone attacks.
